sentences.text: Palaeospheniscus represents an extinct group of penguins placed within the family Spheniscidae.
Members of this genus varied in size, reaching lengths from 55 cm to 73 cm, with the type species being Palaeospheniscus patagonicus.
Moreno and Mercerat named this genus in 1891 based on fossils from Argentine Patagonia.
Most remains come from Santa Cruz and Chubut provinces, though the holotype is a single tarsometatarsus from the Gaiman Formation.
Several other Patagonian genera are now considered part of the three species within Palaeospheniscus.
These birds lived between the Aquitanian and Zanclean stages, spanning roughly 23.04 to 3.6 million years ago.
Fossils also appear in the Miocene to Pliocene of Chile and South Africa, as well as the Oligocene to Miocene of Peru.
